newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent makes modest gains led by firm gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent makes modest gains led by firm gasoline.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures edged higher on Tuesday as U.S. gasoline, the seasonal leader of the oil complex, made strong opening gains.
September Brent was 12 cents up at $18.53 a barrel at 1530 GMT, off a high of $18.65, while August gas oil was up 50 cents at $167.25 a tonne.

NYMEX August gasoline, which expires on Thursday, climbed more than one cent a gallon in the first hour of trade, building on recent gains made amid tight supplies of methyl tertiary butane ether (MTBE).
MTBE is a key blending component used in converting conventional unleaded to reformulated gasoline, the grade deliverable against the NYMEX contract.
"Gasoline is the main leader at the moment, and it's gone roaring up again," said one broker.
"There nothing else leading the market, we're literally just following whatever gasoline does," he added.
News that Exxon Corp had shut its 110,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker at its 411,000 bpd Baytown, Texas refinery after a lightening strike had lent more support to gasoline, brokers said.
Traders were expecting weekly U.S. stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), due after the close of trade, to show a draw on gasoline stocks of between one and three million barrels.

Next resistance for Brent was seen at $18.67 a barrel. Chartists said that gas oil remained well above trendline support in the lows $160s, but needed to break convincingly above $168 to go much higher.
No fresh news on the timing of the resumption of Iraqi exports emerged on Tuesday.
Iraq has submitted to the United Nations all the annexes to its aid plan, the last step before the U.N. can approve the plan and moves towards resuming oil exports can begin.
The U.N. late last week ruled out moving the June 8 start date for Iraqi sales under the oil-for-food plan, a senior official said on Monday.
This would mean the Iraqis could be attempting to sell up to $1 billion worth of crude by September 5.
